prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
The Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System operates amid dry fuels, steep terrain, variable winds, lightning, human-caused ignitions, and expanding wildland-urban interface exposure. Its operational area includes ridgelines, drainages, access roads, utility corridors, remote recreation areas, and communities; small ignitions can become life-safety incidents within minutes.
System elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall) is the shared operating environment presenting incident information, recommended actions, and operational status to authorized wildfire personnel. North Lookout Camera Mast and South Lookout Camera Mast provide fixed observation coverage of high-risk sectors for rapid assessment of smoke columns, flame growth, and visibility changes. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock and Drone Tasking Service support directed aerial observation when fixed views are inconclusive, terrain obstructs sight, or incident staff require updated scene awareness. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine and Smoke Classifier Module screen imagery and other observations for potential fire activity; outputs are decision support, not authoritative findings. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node contributes localized weather context for spread potential, aviation feasibility, firefighter exposure, and field-operation timing. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater bridges digital coordination and field radio practices beyond reliable broadband coverage.
Actors: participating local fire agencies, county emergency management, state wildland fire resources, aviation support units, and cooperating public safety partners have assigned incident responsibilities. County Emergency Liaison represents public-warning, road-impact, shelter, and emergency-operations coordination needs. Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion) monitors detection cues, requests verification, and recommends escalation; may recommend Confirmed Ignition State only when available observations and operating procedures support it. Air Attack Supervisor uses fire location, smoke behavior, aircraft constraints, and resource priorities before advising aerial tactics. Tanker Base Manager uses mission demand, loading status, and operational tempo associated with Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console, East Retardant Loading Pump, and West Retardant Loading Pump.

New part:
S015: The Helitack Crew Leader and Drone Pilot Operator use the system to maintain shared awareness of field conditions, mission timing, and hazards that could affect crew safety.
S016: The Crewline Mobile Tablet provides mobile access to approved operational information for personnel who need current situational awareness away from a command workstation.
S017: Supported decisions include whether a smoke report warrants verification, whether an ignition should be treated as confirmed, whether aerial observation is justified, and whether changing conditions require adjusted priorities.
S018: Supported suppression decisions include where to focus initial attack planning, when to request aviation coordination, which field resources need updated information, and whether operations should pause for safety reasons.
S019: The system also supports recognition of an Airspace Restricted State so that aviation and drone activity can be coordinated under the applicable incident rules.
S020: Detection support begins with observation, automated screening, operator review, and presentation of confidence, location, and context for suspected fire activity.
S021: Detection support ends at the point where an authorized role accepts, rejects, or requests further verification of a suspected ignition under agency procedure.
S022: Suppression support begins after incident staff need coordinated information for resource movement, aviation planning, field safety, and ongoing assessment of fire behavior.
S023: Suppression support does not include autonomous dispatch, independent command decisions, or direct control of aircraft, vehicles, pumps, cameras, drones, or field crews.
S024: Command authority remains with the designated incident command structure, and the system is limited to timely information presentation, procedural support, traceable recommendations, and operational coordination aids.
S025: The system architecture is organized around fixed ridge sensors, a staffed operations portal, advisory analytics services, and communications paths that preserve incident command authority.
S026: North Lookout Camera Mast is positioned on the northern rim of the operating area to provide long-range visual coverage of drainages, access roads, and known ignition corridors.
S027: South Lookout Camera Mast covers the opposing viewshed and provides overlapping observation where terrain breaks line of sight from the northern site.
S028: Each camera mast is installed with hardened power distribution, local equipment cabinets, lightning protection, and service access suitable for seasonal maintenance windows.
S029: The camera mast video paths are backhauled through licensed wireless links to the operations network, with cellular service available as a degraded-mode path where coverage permits.
S030: North Lookout Camera Mast sends the Thermal Spot Snippet after local sensor processing identifies a candidate heat signature.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
